Melilotus messanensis (L.) All., Fl. Pedem. 1:309. 1785. Chamb.in Davis, Fl. Turk. 3:449. 1970; Hansen in Tutin et al, Fl. Europaea 2:150. 1968. Annual, erect or ascending, up to 40 cm. Leaflets ovate-orbicular or lanceolate-cuneate, serrate. Stipules of lower leaves dentate. Inflorescence a raceme, up to 1 cm long, 3-10-flowered, shorter than the subtending leaf. Corolla 4-5 mm, yellow, vexillum and keel subequal, longer than the wings. Fruit 5-8 mm long, concentrically striated, acute. Fl.Per.: February-March. Type: Described from Europe, Herb. Linn. 930/11 (LINN). Distribution: S. Europe, W. Syria, Cyprus, N. Africa, S. Iran, Pakistan (Karachi). Probably a recently introduced weed.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Corolla white; standard 3-5 x 2-4 mm, limb obovate; keel 2.5-3.5 mm long. Pod turgid to slightly compressed; ovoid, 3-4 x 2 mm, glabrous, reticulate to rugose. Seeds 1 or 2.

An occasional weed of cultivation and waste places on the Coastal Plain between Coolup and Bullsbrook. Also recorded for Albany, Beverley and Esperance. Introduced, native to Europe and Asia.

Flowers October-February.

*M. indica* (L.) All. — King Island Melilot, Hexham Scent

Erect or sprawling annual or biennial herb 0.1-0.5 m high; stems angular, more or less glabrous. Stipules subulate, entire or 1 or 2-toothed towards the base. Leaflets obovate or narrowly obovate, 5-26 x 3-15 mm, glabrous above, sparsely pilose below, truncate to emarginate and often minutely apiculate, margins serrulate. Racemes dense, 10-40 mm long; peduncle 10-30 mm long, erect. Calyx tube 0.5-1 mm long; lobes triangular, 0.5-1.5 mm long. Corolla yellow; standard 2.5-3 x 1-1.5 mm, limb narrowly obovate; keel 2-2.5 mm long. Pod turgid to very slightly compressed, ovoid to almost globular, 2-3 x 1.5-2 mm, reticulate to rugose, 1-seeded.

Naturalized on the Coastal Plain throughout the Perth Region from Bunbury to Gingin. Extends north to Kalbarri and south to the extreme south west and Esperance. Native to the Mediterranean Region.

Flowers mainly August-October.

Contains coumarin which taints milk and eggs, when eaten by cows and poultry.

*M. messanensis* (L.) All. — Messina Melilot

Erect or sprawling, glabrous to sparsely pilose annual herb; stems rather succulent. Stipules with a subulate apex, but obliquely dilated and toothed towards the base, margins dentate.
